newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesians flock to polls in general election.
newsitem.headline: Indonesians flock to polls in general election.

text.p: Millions of Indonesians flocked to the polls on Thursday in national and local elections through the sprawling archipelago of more than 17,500 islands.
Lines had formed outside polling stations in Jakarta well before voting started at 8 a.m. (0100 GMT) under clear sunny skies.
Polls close at 2 p.m. (0700 GMT) with the ruling Golkar, in power for most of President Suharto's 30-year rule, assured of a comfortable victory.

Political analysts said they were watching to see if the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), which launched a strong challenge to Golkar during the most violent election campaign in 30 years, would increase its share of the vote.
Golkar won 68 percent in the last elections in 1992 and is pushing to get just over 70 percent this time around.

The PPP won 17 percent in 1992 and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), now badly split over a leadership struggle, 15 percent. The three parties are the only ones legally entitled to contest the elections
Nearly 125 million people are eligible to vote on Thursday in the world's fourth most populous nation.
President Suharto appealed in an election-eve address on Wednesday night for people to vote as their democratic right and duty.
